notes.title: Skill-Based Character System & Post-Game Overhaul! (v. FR 2.03.000)
notes.content:
Hello all,

Two major road map items are complete and included in our latest patch! We performed a complete overhaul of our character \ RPG system, and additionally made some significant game flow changes that are most evident in the post-game info page (this is actually a bonus roadmap item).

Essentially, these changes both cleanup some of the messiest areas of the game, and also pivot the game & the player toward a deeper sense of belonging in the Mugalo Galaxy. There were various elements in the game that were very intense and heavily focused on survival and permadeath. While we like how these elements raised the stakes & excitement, they also were detracting from a really calm & relaxing exploration experience. 

These changes also pave the way for the future, allowing us to expand the game vertically using the new character skill system. These skills will allow us to establish a deeper progression into farming, fishing, and potentially harpooning. 

Anyway, without elaborating the reasons for every single change, here are the highlights / specifics:

[b]Game-Flow Changes[/b]
[list]
[*] The player now starts with very few credits and a VFlare ship. New ships may be bought with acquired credits over time.
[*] Scoring has been removed from the game. You will still get a post-game report (see below), but the constant pressure to maintain a score is gone.
[*] Names of the difficulty levels have been changed.
[*] The final game report is now based on clear inputs and a fewer number of inputs, these are summarized in a graphical color bar (see below).
[*] This final rating is primarily based on progressed skills, surviving family members, reaching Lilith, and the initial difficulty level (time is no longer a factor). No rush to reach Lilith!
[*] All of the post-game statistic graphs have been fixed!
[/list]

[b]Skill-Based Character System[/b]
[list]
[*] Instead of the six old skills, each character now has only three skills (fishing, farming, and spacefaring).
[*] These skills are dynamic, as discrete actions in gameplay will progress them.
[*] Each skill has seven levels, and each new level will provide the player with new rewards such as new fish, farming perks, and spacefaring perks.
[*] The blood volume and lung gas graphs have been removed.
[*] The sleep and workout sliders have been removed.
[*] Farming EXP can be acquired by researching farming technologies or growing crops.
[*] Fishing EXP can be acquired by catching fish and attempting to catch fish.
[*] Spacefaring EXP can be acquired by researching spacefaring technologies or by flying through the Mugalo Galaxy.
[/list]

You can read much more about the details of these two updates in our issue tracking system:
https://github.com/chaystarjun/LilithCommunityTracker/issues/123 
https://github.com/chaystarjun/LilithCommunityTracker/issues/124

[b]The Character Skills Screen[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/SUAsWrU.png[/img]

[b]The New Post-Game Report[/b]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/IkB8vUa.png[/img]

Best,
-john and pete


[b][u]New Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Skill-Based Character System!
[*] Post-Game Overhaul!
[/list]
[b][u]Polish[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Flight UI & raiding screen fonts cleaned up.
[*] Positive health conditions show boosts when hovering.
[*] It's no longer possible to start with a ship that does not have enough signal strength to complete the tutorial.
[/list]

[b][u]Roadmap Update[/u][/b]

We made a few small changes to the road map. Things are becoming a clearer to us, and so we've adjusted accordingly. "Science & Experiments", for now, is unlikely to ever happen -- there really was no clear vision for that, haha. Therefore, you'll see it is marked "Cancelled". Also, the most recent road-map item, the "Post-Game Overhaul", is a sudden arrival. This was a major change to the game, and we felt it was important to the game's flow, so we added it to the road map and finished it at the same time. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/P11N39L.png[/img]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 2.01.002)
notes.content:
Hey all,

We were able to address one major community desire (autosave), and snuck in a few other updates. Regarding the "color corrections", the game was originally developed on monitors with a rare gamma setting -- so during development, to us, the game appeared bright, more colorful, and more of a pastel palette. But, we later realized how rare our monitors were, which means that about 95% of our users were experiencing a much darker version of the game. This patch delivers the game colors as we intended with the help of some color correction scripts. We also added autosave which will occur every five minutes. There is no option to turn autosave on or off, it will always be on. There is also no in-game notification of autosave, but if you go to the main menu, you should see that saves are being established every five minutes. 

Additionally, with the release of Proton, we believe our game is now compatible with Linux -- so we'll be relying on that avenue for Linux support instead of making a dedicated Linux build. 

Finally, for those who are not aware, our Soundtrack was released a while back and can now be downloaded from our store page. I believe users who already bought the game will get the soundtrack's cheaper bundle price as if they had bought the two together.

Best,
-john & pete

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Lilith Odyssey now has Linux support via Proton.
[*] Soundtrack Released.
[*] Autosave (occurs every 5 minutes).
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] All game colors corrected to match original artistic vision.
[*] Planet view menu buttons have been moved to the center of the screen to avoid overlapping clutter.
[/list]

notes.title: The IGG Small Goods Marketplace (v. EA 1.02.000)
notes.content:
[i]"Citizen. Register your inventories at the kiosk. Exchange your goods, and then exit the trading floor. All transactions are monitored and sanctioned by the IGG." [/i]

This latest update is another large update to the game. The [b]IGG Small Goods Marketplace[/b] is available at all stores & stations throughout the galaxy. Within the small goods marketplace, a variety of items can be bought and sold at market prices. The items that players can buy and sell are listed below, but essentially, the market only allows for transactions on about 20 common items such as Florp, Ammo, Potatoes, or Fuel Cells.

Our goal with this change is to provide a market for future commodities that will be arriving in our upcoming roadmap items. For example, both fishing & farming will provide the player with goods (fish & crops) that should be sellable at a common market. Additionally, this market increases the fluidity & usefulness of money. Players can now use their banks more tangibly to improve their journey to Lilith. Players can also reliability sell fuel cells or farmed items at market prices -- which opens a variety of new play styles.

We also took this opportunity to heavily adjust the prices & resource costs of our mid-game and late-game items (see below). Generally speaking, these mid & late tier items were increased in cost -- we were noticing that the late game items were far too accessible at an early stage.

[b]Roadmap Update[/b]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/QaDmDxY.png[/img]

Welcome to some new community members :D @HEDGEHOG, @PotatoTheScourge

notes.title: Sandbox Mode! (v. EA 1.01.000)
notes.content:
With our first major update since our initial Early Access release, we hope to provide casual gamers with a more suitable and low-key a game mode: [b]Sandbox Mode[/b]. In [i]Survival Mode[/i], players are asked to keep oxygen meters, power meters, and other survival threats at bay. In Sandbox Mode, a number of these hardline mechanics have been removed or dampened (see below for details about what Sandbox Mode actually is). 

Additionally, we laid the foundation for several of our upcoming road map items (road map attached below). Our next update will likely be the addition of an IGG Marketplace (primarily a UI feature) where any resource item \ harvested item can be sold at market prices. This IGG market is critical to our plans for the Fishing Update (selling fish at market price) and our Farming Overhaul (selling crops at market price, among other things). 

[b]Roadmap[/b]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/7PqUv0K.png[/img]

In this release, a few items in the community backlog were also fixed (see below). We are still attempting to refine & polish the game as much as possible -- but of course, we are not a giant game studio, and Lilith will always have its quirks -- to quote one of my favorite game developers, Jonathan Blow, "things that are personal have flaws". 

Community Shout-outs: @jogBrogzin, @sirenderboy, @deexEngima! 

[b][u]Sandbox Mode[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] On the character select screen, players can select "Survival Mode" or "Sandbox Mode".
[*] The power meter is no longer displayed or relevant when in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The oxygen meter is no longer displayed or relevant when in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The space-madness meter is no longer displayed or relevant when in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The Hunger & Starvation conditions do less damage in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The Methane Poisoning condition does less damage in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The Freezing & Overheated conditions will not trigger in Sandbox Mode.
[*] The Asphyxia condition will not trigger in Sandbox Mode.
[*] Bleeding Out, Organ Damage, Bacterial Infections do less damage to the player in Sandbox Mode.
[*] Creatures, Enemies, Combat do less damage to the player in Sandbox Mode.
[*] Thermal Regulation does not apply & will not occur in Sandbox mode.
[*] All actions that typically require power, no longer require power in Sandbox Mode (save game, beam out, turning on planet lamps).
[*] Storms damage the ship less in Sandbox mode.
[*] Ship Raids are slightly less dangerous in Sandbox mode.
[*] The minimum sailing speed (in the case of no fuel) is greatly increased in Sandbox mode -- thus preventing the player from getting overly stranded.
[/list]
[b]Note: [/b]If you are a Sandbox player, and have game-balance ideas, let us know in the discord! We expect it will take some time to get the game mode right.

[b][u]New Visual Changes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The appearance of deep space is now much more colorful & vibrant (it is filled with gaseous entities).
[*] Solar objects look less dark from a distance.
[*] A camera effect will make (not wearing your suit) light-headed related dizzy-ness uncomfortable.
[*] The Interaction Window (Stores, Haggling, Medical Attention, etc.) has been re-organized and visually improved for aesthetic and ease-of-use purposes.
[*] Changed appearance of the condition-healing panel (appears when you click a condition to heal it using EFU resources).
[*] Fuel & Ration status bars in the upper right corner (Resources Panel) have been aesthetically improved.
[*] The O2, Rations, Fuel, and Power Meters will no longer blink excessively when in Survival Mode, they will blink three times and then hold a steady illuminated state.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The minimum sailing speed (in the case of no fuel) was slightly increased in Survival mode as well.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Character heights, when in metric mode, were being displayed as thousands of centimeters instead of ordinary sizes. This should be resolved now.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.023)
notes.content:
In this patch, a number of items in the community backlog were fixed (see below). The biggest changes are the ability to play with metric units enabled, and the minimizing of the tutorial. See below for more details. Thanks for your patience -- we've been taking some time to investigate the feasibility of multiplayer -- and we'll let you know if we think we can pull it off. In the immediate future (possibly the next patch), we'll be looking to add fishing (on planets) to the game. 

Thanks again to the (growing!) community (@matric, @onlyhow, @zzz, @aplethoraof, @Hoxtilicious!, @sirenderboy, @toker, @kilon, @tobugis, @godrow, @deexengima) -- hopefully soon we can start working on some more significant features.

[b][u]New Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Players can now enable the display of [u][b]metric units[/b][/u] by going to the gameplay tab of the settings menu. The choice effects planet temperatures, blood temperatures, character height, and character weight.
[*] The tutorial can be minimized. Some players were having trouble seeing behind the tutorial, or closing it when they were done with reading it.
[/list]

[b][u]Polish[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The performance of opening & closing the map has been improved. It should open pretty quickly now.
[*] Stations no longer say "Cannot Land Here" when docked, they say "Docked".
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] You can now heal \ cure space madness when visiting a store or space station that provides medical care.
[*] You can no longer heal a dead person back to life at a medical station \ store.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] After an end game and then a new game, in addition to resetting the tech tree, we now reset the print catalogue item selections as well (this was always the intent).
[*] Build 1.00.022 broke all of the space UI star \ planet trackers, they've been fixed now.
[*] Player markers no longer appear on the loading screen.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.022)
notes.content:
In this patch, we were able to continue our march through the community backlog. We also corrected some items in our personal backlog. The current focus is still on playability, polish, and balance. On a positive note, the game is pretty stable right now. From this foundation we should be able to start working on some of our own new feature ideas and some of the community requested features. 

Thanks to the community for the continual feedback -- it is helping to improve the game :). 

[b][u]New Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The HUD tracker can now be used on any star or planet regardless of distance. For example, Lilith can be tracked from anywhere in the galaxy.
[*] The HUD tracker will stick to the edges of the screen when facing away from tracked objects (before it would disappear). 
[/list]

[b][u]Polish[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] An indication is now displayed when inside a galactic storm (some user's were confused about why their camera was shaking or were given little warning about their entry into a storm).
[*] An indication is now displayed when inside a planet or star (to avoid confusion regarding the camera effects that occur while inside planets).
[*] A UI key-bind indication was added to the materialize-building UI suggesting to the player that they may press R to rotate their building (it was not obvious to players that buildings could be rotated).
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Braking speed has been increased.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] When loading saved games creatures & plants will not be re-discovered in a way that contributes to a user's steam-achievement statistics.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.021)
notes.content:
This patch mainly focused on polish & some strange issues that we noticed in streams. We're also just generally working through a larger bug log, and trying to fine tune our game mechanics, area by area. This patch will initiate some changes to the handling of spacecraft, that will likely take some time to completely tune.

Thanks to @pizzbonez, @sirenderboy, @retromation, @DeexEnigma, @Saracen for identifying these :).

[h3]Side Announcement![/h3]
Congratulations to @Pizzabonez for setting the first official Lilith Odyssey Speed running record! His in-game time was pretty low (20.5 Voyage Days)! If you'd like to make an attempt at breaking the record, be sure to capture a video (YouTube \ twitch) of your run, so that it can be verified officially.

[b][u]New Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The planet camera angle can now be adjusted permanently. It will not snap back when you release middle-mouse.
[*] The space camera angle can also be adjusted permanently. To snap it back, the player is able to press "V" (which is also shown as an indicator as soon as the camera angle is altered).
[*] The Navigation Ball (B) now displays a brighter red dot, and this dot is labelled as the player's target. This target is helpful for navigating to far-away destinations.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Having items breakdown for additional resources at a 1.8 rate was breaking our underlying economy (as breakdown rates are percentages of the printing costs (with our 3 different EFU techs)). Instead of adjusting this coefficient (from 1.0 to 1.8) we increased the likelihood of loot drops by a factor of 2.0. The end result is about the same.
[*] Space Madness will now decrease while players are on planets, and increase while in space (instead of permanently increasing while in space). We may raise or lower the rates of these processes in the future.
[*] Braking & Engine controls have been normalized. Controls were formerly tied to a user's frame-rate or machine performance (which created undesirable quickness or slowness for these controls). From here, we can balance the speeds of these controls based on community feedback.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] The in-game Manual no longer has images cut-off by the scrollbar.
[*] The title screen "LILITH" text will no longer be hidden on various systems that had an issue.
[*] The tech-tree text was disappearing for some users due to toggling the UI to LARGE mode. This has been fixed.
[*] The character information screen now says "Methane" instead of "Meth".
[*] Storms should no longer be generated within 95 LY of the home-world systems.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.020)
notes.content:
So it seems like some of our ease-of-play economic balance changes may have gone overboard. This patch brings them closer to the ideal values (hopefully).  We also fixed a few save-game bugs, and some game-polish issues.

Thanks to @DeexEnigma, @Voxel, @Saracen, @wandtpag, @syllospri, @Wolfram, @GachaPawn for identifying these :).

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fuel efficiency in space decreased from [b]2.2[/b] to [b]1.5[/b].
[*] Harvested Resources (such as dirt or logs) breakdown rate is now 1.8x. You may notice some decimals in the UI, the EFU actually stores data with decimal precision, but the UI may hide that precision at times.
[*] Potato Farms now generate 8 potatoes per florp canister (instead of 10).
[*] Warp Root Farms now generate 5 warp roots per florp canister (instead of 6).
[*] Protium Fuel Wells now generate 8 protium cells per battery (instead of 10).
[*] Deuterium Fuel Wells now generate 5 deuterium cells per battery (instead of 6).
[*] Potatoes, Warp Root, and Nitrocorn now convert to to less fuel (1,2,3 grams of fuel) per food item respectively. This is intended to prevent exploits where players completely ignore the production of fuel cells.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Save games were failing to load due to an issue regarding file paths. Should be corrected now. Also, the save-game feature is probably one of the least tested features, so bear with us as we handle a potential range of game-saving issues in early access. We hope to iron these out prior to the full release.
[*] Fixed a bug where the tutorial text did not match the tutorial objectives when tracking the initial star.
[*] Jazzgore loading screen spelling mistake corrected.
[*] Printing 5 fuel cells during the tutorial should now count as 5 fuel instead of 1. It was intended that folks would generate the cells using a fuel rig, but it is equally acceptable to print them.
[/list]

notes.title: Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.019)
notes.content:
Most of the changes in this patch were directed at making the game more playable and friendly for new players. Our development testers got pretty good at the game (due to playing so frequently, haha) -- so, in this patch, we notched the difficulty back quite a bit. We may have taken it too far, but if so, we'll keep adjusting until we find a steady balance. Thanks for you patience and support :).

Thanks to @Saracen, @peasantsi (Twitch), @wandtpag, @syllospri, @Wolfram for identifying their issues & requests on launch day.

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fuel efficiency in space increased by a factor of [b]2.2[/b].
[*] Harvested Resources (such as dirt or logs) now breakdown down into 2x as many EFU resources (carbon, metal, nanite).
[*] Potato Farms now generate 10 potatoes per florp canister (instead of 4).
[*] Warp Root Farms now generate 6 warp roots per florp canister (instead of 3).
[*] Nitrocorn Farms now generate 3 nitro-corn per florp canister (instead of 2).
[*] Solar Beacons now generate 2 batteries per cycle (instead of 1).
[*] Protium Fuel Wells now generate 10 protium cells per battery (instead of 4).
[*] Deuterium Fuel Wells now generate 6 deuterium cells per battery (instead of 3).
[*] Tritium Fuel Wells now generate 3 tritium cells per battery (instead of 2).
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an an issue where survival gear (crates, farms, rigs) still existed if you beamed back onto a planet (2 copies would exist -- the ones in your inventory and the one on the planet). Our save-game code, and beam-up code (for saving a planet state) were using the same code. When saving games, we want to save rigs and such on planets, but not when beaming up! Thanks for finding this @syllospri.
[/list]

notes.title: Finally! Lilith Odyssey is Launching this Friday!
notes.content:
[h2]Finally done![/h2]
We are happy to announce that we are locked in for a launch of the game, this Friday, August 20th! It has been a really long time for us. As a pair of game-developers who have worked on this project for five years while simultaneously holding full-time day jobs -- we are thrilled to be able to deliver this game to you. It's going to be both an exciting and an emotional moment for us. We really hope you enjoy the game -- and we hope your feedback will continue to roll in, which helps us bring the game to higher levels.

[h2]Launch Discount & New Features[/h2]
For the first 7 days, we'll be offering a launch discount of 23%! We'll be releasing version (EA 1.00.018), and incrementing from this baseline. A number of exciting new features have been implemented since the demo, and many bugs \ polish issues have been addressed. 

[h2]Development Notes (v. EA 1.00.018)[/h2]
After the demo event, we began working on a number of significant issues & features identified by the community. Thanks community! We will continue to implement your ideas & suggestions.

Special thanks to @DeexEnigma,  @Narkulus, @Nookrium, @pel, @RehabSubmarine, @Evan9808, @hawkeye, @ShadowKnightEX, @xerxes8169, @Kojimin, @SekansAval, and @Pizzabonez who identified many issues that we were able to resolve before the launch! 

[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Ship: The StarCruise 550
[*] New Ship: The Jerbis Freight Class
[*] Planet Camera can now be rotated using middle mouse (the space camera already had this ability).
[*] Standard Planet Camera now angled behind player, no longer birds-eye view (looks much nicer).
[*] Games can now be saved.
[*] The game can be paused now (activating the Tab-Screen will not pause the game).
[*] Manual is now cleaner and easier to read (fewer text walls, more pictures, more direct language used to identify key actions player needs to know).
[*] Player's suit now performs thermal regulation when on exceptionally cold or hot worlds. This requires battery power. If battery power is lost, thermal regulation will stop, and the player may overheat or freeze to death.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Distances between home planets and initial stars were adjusted. We want that distance to be about 14 LY for now, but may adjust after depending on the community's input.
[*] Galaxy now has many more animals, raiders, and civilizations (less vacuous). 
[*] Sailing is faster & more fuel efficient.
[*] Farms now much more efficient during the day, and less efficient at night.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where space-raids could crash the game.
[*] Resolved an issue where the tutorial would randomly close after exactly 7 in-game days.
[*] Resolved a bug where the macro "%offer_item%" was not replaced during trade encounters.
[*] Planet items, such as farms and crates are now correctly reloaded after a game-save and load.
[*] Storm sound no longer continues when a player beams down to a planet from a space storm.
[*] Tutorial flow issues resolved (skipping steps, inaccessible objectives, etc.)
[/list]

[b][u]Polish[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Added info about Power Usage to the manual.
[*] Added Combat information to the manual.
[*] Made ration-converting information more clear in the manual.
[*] Native spu given unique technologic uniforms.
[*] Lilith surface (the target planet) has been adjusted significantly. 
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 14.0
notes.content:
In Beta 14.0 we resolved a handful of high priority bugs that were identified in beta testing. The experience continues to get smoother, and our bug log is looking a bit smaller. 

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Allowed the player to put their suit on at any time regardless of the planet type. Suits are required on worlds without quality atmospheres.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Civilians can no longer be killed by the player (and therefore cannot be harvested for resources). 
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Pure water worlds can now be reached by the player.
[*] Player can now move items between the ship part inventory (ship configuration) and their back pack \ tools inventory.
[*] Ship parts are now correctly removed from the ship when they are destroyed by a storm or raid.
[*] Planets no longer display "-Infinity" as the current temperature.
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] UI trackers can be selected again (this was broken by a previous build).
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 12.6
notes.content:
In Beta 12.6 we are working through a few errors we have in the underlying unity framework. We also reworked the tutorial, and added support for ultrawide screens.

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Added support for ultra-wide aspect ratios.
[*] Tutorial has been extensively reworked.
[*] Upgraded to a stable version of unity.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] None.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] None.
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] UI elements subdivided across multiple canvases to increase UI performance.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 12.0
notes.content:
In Beta 12.0 we dealt with a few setbacks -- but ultimately worked through these newly discovered problems fairly quickly. We also still found time to add a few features that help round out the overall experience.

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Health conditions can now be cured if the player has enough resources, using 3D printed medicines. 
[*] The galaxy stars have been reorganized into their final configuration. Galaxy appears more spiral-like now.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Sending family members on resource gathering missions will now cost rations.
[*] Storms now cause more damage to ships.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Ultralong beamdown lag was discovered to be associated with having multiple perks active, and has been resolved.
[*] Some planets & stations in space were incorrectly catalogue in the internal database, causing a crash. 
[*] Space stations no longer attempt to load twice (causing bugs and lag).
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Infinity treaty monument had wrong Y coordinate and was being rendered several hundred light years above the plane of the galaxy. 
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 11.0
notes.content:
In Beta 11.0 several bugs & stability issues have been addressed. We've fixed 101 issues to-date. Our current burndown list has only 26 items, but we expect that to grow as Beta test evolves into the future.  Our efforts have transitioned more toward fine tuning & balancing -- which is always good to see. With our small can't promise a totally bug free experience at first, but we our committed to making the experience as smooth as possible!

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Dangerous creatures & enemies will now longer spawn directly near players who beam down to planets.
[*] Print menu now loads much faster!
[*] Farms and Fuel Rigs will now play a sound when a batch of resources has finished generating\processing.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Tech tree prices have been greatly increased to slow the vertical progress of the player through the game's high end equipment.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Lag & glitches no longer occurring when flying near the black hole.
[*] Additionally discovered beam-down crashes have been fixed.
[*] Weather cells now accurate correlated with weather cells on the map.
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Great Red Moopzoi's HP bar is now at the correct height (will not clip through the tree).
[*] Fixed an issue where element breakdowns were displaying an inaccurate message regarding resources acquired in the breakdown.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 10.0
notes.content:
In Beta 10.0 a number of bugs & stability issues have been addressed. Additionally, we are working on a comprehensive balancing of the fuel economy -- to standardize the planet hopping experience. Tank sizes, fuel efficiencies, and fuel production rates must all be considered! 

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Fuel production economy and burn rates overhauled to optimize the planet hopping experience.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Creatures across the board are slightly more lethal.
[*] Florp now costs 15 carbon.
[*] Solar Beacons are more expensive now.
[*] Solar Beacons produce batteries slightly faster now.
[*] Raids occur much more frequently now (when in raiding zones) -- as desired.
[*] Warping is less efficient.
[*] Sailing is much faster and much more viable.
[*] Inventory auto-conversion of fuel is no longer in the settings menu.
[*] Fuel Tanks are much larger.
[*] All ships start with only 70 fuel.
[*] Fuel cells convert to less fuel.
[*] Ships move 30% slower.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Item Avatar Pool was ballooning and causing performance issues.
[*] Now able to Press 'F' at monuments and other sites and view the associated info messages.
[*] Pressing 'S' to stop the ship now retracts the sails at a slightly higher speed -- to make flight more intuitive.
[*] Ship steering not moves free from the framerate, making slightly lower framerates much more tolerable in space.
[*] Dead zones and Raider Zones now use conical detection instead of spherical detection so that they trigger as desired.
[*] Test enemies removed from Bmunji.
[*] Organelles and fruits are now easier to chop (chopping radius expanded).
[*] Zop Trusts now has items and contracts available.
[*] Medical attention window now renders correctly when first accessed. 
[*] When you have a negative amount of a resource (unlikely to begin with) you can now still buy items for which you have enough resources.
[*] Multiple technologies cannot be quickly researched even when the required resources for them do not exist.
[*] Swapping Items between backpack and ship inventory no longer destroys items in the backpack.
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Floating trash and sea objects are no longer appearing in the sky.
[*] Jazgore & Wojtek's descriptions updated on the planet loading screens.
[*] Dame Voltara's bottom sails were being rendered upside down.
[*] UI warning now displayed (with audio alert) when in a raider zone.
[*] Rock names are now all set to "Nutrient Rock" instead of internal code names.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 9.3
notes.content:
Beta Test marches on. We are addressing the most significant stability issues, and also various easy-to-fix minor issues that exist in related areas.

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] None.
[/list]

[b][u]Balance[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Player no longer awarded points for buying items at stores.
[*] Adjusted the ranges of difficulty levels.
[*] Beam down cooldown is now 20s.
[*] Beam up cooldown is now 20s.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Buildings (Gear) is no removed from planets when the player beams up. Previously, the gear was cloned (existed on both planet & in the player inventory.
[*] De-materializing (un-placing) gear no longer destroys the items contained inside.
[*] Several game-crashes associated with beaming down have been averted. 
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Water-splashes correctly colored now.
[*] Rotated buildings are now placed with the intended rotation.
[*] Bullet accuracy is now displayed correctly in game statistics data.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta 9.1
notes.content:
The team is progressing through beta test! We are addressing various issues that have been identified. 

[b][u]Features[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] UI Windows, such as the Tech Tree and Print Catalogue can now be closed.
[*] Animals now fight back (at varying probabilities) when they are attacked.
[*] Destruction blocks (blood blocks) no longer fade away immediately.
[/list]

[b][u]Bug Fixes[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] When buying a ship, all data fields are no longer zero.
[*] Lag that caused planet mode rotations to drop framerate \ skip has been addressed.
[*] Generating of destruction blocks no longer causes small amount of lag.
[*] Grenade kills no longer create a large lagged voxel explosion.
[/list]

[b][u]Visual Tweaks[/u][/b]
[list]
[*] Ships rotated 45 degrees on the ship purchasing UI.
[*] Larger ships now fit within the UI window.
[*] Ship management visualization no longer clips through the galaxy map.
[/list]
